records.text: A 2007 investigation found that Richard William Erpenbeck failed to tell the Bank of Corbin about existing mortgages, causing it to issue loans on four already-encumbered properties.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: But they didn't. We learned that in 2007, they then opened an investigation into him for the following reasons. Reason number one is because while employed by the Bank of Corbin to perform title searches on certain properties, Rick (Richard William Erpenbeck) didn't inform the bank that other mortgages already existed on those properties. ... So they were issuing loans to multiple people for the same property, right? This means a failure to disclose this information resulted in the Bank of Corbin issuing loans on four of the properties that were already encumbered by pre-existing mortgages.

verification.notes: The Kentucky Supreme Court opinion states Erpenbeck failed to learn that Bank of Corbin held existing mortgages, leading four properties to be encumbered by both the bank mortgages and later loans.

sources.title: Richard Erpenbeck v. Kentucky Bar Association
sources.relevance: Kentucky Supreme Court opinion confirms the existing mortgages and four doubly encumbered properties.
